sources.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas converted to x^0 = c t
sources.locator: Sections 4.2-4.6 pp. 82-120: Section 4.2 pp. 82-83 (emission derivation and the exact E = m gamma c^2, kinetic energy m(gamma-1)), Sections 4.3.1-4.3.6 pp. 88-102 (energy-momentum vector, collision invariants, examples, momentum-velocity relation, massless particles, massless-particle evidence), Section 4.4 pp. 101-103 (systems with internal structure), Section 4.5 pp. 103-106 (four-force, force measured by an observer, work) and Section 4.6 pp. 106-120 (applications, read for disposition only); printed page numbers as in the PDF text layer

contents.name: Section 4.2 pp. 82-83: the exact particle identities E = m gamma c^2 and kinetic energy m(gamma - 1)
contents.support: The exact energy and kinetic-energy formulas in terms of the coordinate velocity are absorbed into clause (b) of the four-momentum frame lemma, where they are derived from P = mU rather than from the source's emission argument.

contents.name: Section 4.2 pp. 82-83: Einstein's emission derivation of E = mc^2
contents.reason: The source itself records that this derivation uses a low-velocity approximation and hidden assumptions and repairs it later through stress-energy; the framework here adopts P = mU and derives the mass shell algebraically, so the emission argument is not used as a proof route.

contents.name: Section 4.3.1 pp. 88-89: energy-momentum is a four-vector; m^2 = E^2 - p^2 and (mc^2)^2 = E^2 - (pc)^2 as the relativistic definition of mass
contents.support: The observer energy, spatial momentum and invariant mass of a four-momentum are defined exactly as the model quantities E_n(P) = -c eta(P,n), q_n(P) = h(P) and m(P) = sqrt(-eta(P,P))/c; the source's heuristic linearity argument for the four-vector character is replaced by the model identification P = mU with the transformation law of the tensor theorem.

contents.name: Section 4.3.1 p. 89, self-check A: interpretation of m^2 = E^2 - p^2 at m = 0
contents.support: The degenerate case is answered by the separate massless-particle premise (nonzero future null momentum, not mU at m = 0) and by the explicit counterexample ex-sr-massless-momentum-not-mu-at-zero-mass; the source's own formula is not extended to m = 0.

contents.name: Section 4.3.2 p. 90, Example 7: two opposite light waves have total momentum (2E, 0) and collective mass 2E
contents.support: The worked example recomputes the collective invariant mass of oppositely directed null momenta exactly, with E_1 = E_2 and with unequal energies, and records the parallel case as a null total with no rest frame.

contents.name: Section 4.3.2 p. 90: collision invariants, centre-of-mass frame, M^2 = (p1+p2)^2 = m1^2 + m2^2 + 2 p1 . p2 and M >= m1 + m2
contents.support: The centre-of-momentum identity Mc^2 = sum E, the per-side inequality M >= sum m, its equality case, the two-leg formula M^2 = m1^2 + m2^2 + 2 m2 E / c^2 and the necessary threshold inequality are all proved for conserving on-shell data; the reversed-triangle inequality is replaced by the exact observer-energy argument.

contents.name: Section 4.3.3 p. 91, Example 8: velocity from energy and momentum, v = p / E
contents.support: Clause (b) gives p = m gamma_w w and E = m gamma_w c^2, hence w = c^2 p / E in the source's c = 1 form; the derivation is the model's own and needs no additional source claim.

contents.name: Section 4.3.3 pp. 91-92, Example 9: light rays do not interact
contents.reason: The source restricts the claim to rays without wave structure and its determinism/symmetry argument is incomplete; the reader report records that energy-momentum alone permits noncollinear outgoing pairs. Classical wave superposition belongs to the electromagnetic wave page, and the purely kinematic one-null-leg impossibility is proved here in lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions (d).

contents.name: Section 4.3.3 p. 92, Example 10: beta-decay angular-momentum selection rule
contents.reason: The claim requires nuclear spin, the weak interaction and measured beta-decay spectra, none of which is available in this classical framework without quantum postulates and primary empirical reports.

contents.name: Section 4.3.3 pp. 93-94, Example 11: Compton scattering and the 478 keV Compton edge
contents.reason: The example is quantum photon-electron scattering with a measured detector spectrum; the reader report records a printed lambda-shift defect, and any faithful account needs a quantum model plus a primary experimental report, so it cannot be scaffolded here.

contents.name: Section 4.3.3 p. 94, Example 12: one-photon pair production cannot happen in vacuum
contents.support: Clause (d) proves the exact kinematic statement that a conserving on-shell datum with a single incoming null leg and any massive outgoing leg does not exist; the reader-confirmed restriction to the one-photon process (two-photon pair production is kinematically allowed) is respected.

contents.name: Section 4.3.4 p. 96: momentum-velocity relation p = m gamma v and the four-vector form p = mv
contents.support: Clause (b) proves p = m gamma_w w for a massive particle in a chart, with the four-vector normalisation carrying the gamma factor, and the worked example ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths checks the exact rational case.

contents.name: Section 4.3.4 p. 96, Figure g and its caption: high-precision experimental verification of p = m gamma v (Meyer et al. 1963)
contents.reason: A faithful empirical account needs the primary report, apparatus and field calibration, electron energy measurement, sampling model and uncertainties; the design of the experimental-interface page reserves exactly such a primary-report queue and authors no experiment from secondary summaries.

contents.name: Section 4.3.5 pp. 96-97: massless particles travel at c, have no rest frame, and p = m gamma v is an indeterminate form as m -> 0
contents.support: The massless model premise describes the particle by a nonzero future null four-momentum, explicitly not mU for any m >= 0, with no four-velocity, proper time or rest frame; the model's v = c statement is the null character together with the separate ideal-light-ray premise.

contents.name: Section 4.3.6 pp. 97-102: empirical evidence as to which particles are massless (neutrino history, photon and graviton mass bounds)
contents.reason: Particle-physics mass bounds rest on quantum fields and on primary experimental publications with instrument and statistical analysis; no such empirical claim is authored in this framework.

contents.name: Section 4.4 pp. 101-103: systems with internal structure, the bead-wire counterexample, isolated-system conservation, stress-energy required for a general proof
contents.reason: Composite and extended systems, their total four-momentum and the stress-energy tensor are the declared subject of the forces-and-continuum pair, whose design reserves the divergence-free total stress and finite-flux arguments; this page treats point particles and their finite collision data only.

contents.name: Section 4.5.1 p. 103: four-force F = ma = dp/d tau, defined only for massive particles
contents.support: The proper-time derivative of the four-momentum and the name four-force are defined exactly, with no force law adopted; the identity F = mA for a C^2 worldline with constant mass is proved in the four-force identities lemma.

contents.name: Section 4.5.2 pp. 103-104: the force measured by an observer, F_o = dp/dt, its three-force part and the timelike power component
contents.support: Clauses (b) and (c) prove dE/dt = f . w and F = gamma (f . w / c, f) for the coordinate three-force f = dp/dt, which is exactly the source's observer-measured force and its power component.

contents.name: Section 4.5.3 p. 105: transformation rules for the measured force, F'_parallel = F_parallel and F'_perp = F_perp / gamma
contents.reason: These rules are a derived consequence of the four-vector transformation of the force and are not a promised claim of this pair; the framework supplies the four-vector component law instead, and the source's derivation is restricted to boosts parallel or perpendicular to the force.

contents.name: Section 4.5.4 pp. 105-106: work relation dE/dx = F and dE/dp = p/E = v
contents.support: Clause (b), dE/dt = f . w, is the rate form of the source's work-kinetic-energy relation for the coordinate three-force; the accompanying derivative dE/dp = p/E follows from the mass shell of the observer identities lemma.

contents.name: Section 4.6 pp. 106-120: applications (Stefan-Boltzmann law, radiation equation of state, thermodynamics and stellar applications, tachyon searches)
contents.reason: These applications need thermodynamics, radiation models, quantum statistics or dedicated empirical searches from other frameworks, and the reader report identifies the quantum and thermodynamic supplements as not consequences of special relativity.

sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997); PDF page = printed page + 7
sources.locator: Chapter 1, printed pp. 27-30 (PDF pp. 34-37): equations (1.98)-(1.102) on printed p. 27 (four-velocity, energy-momentum four-vector, force four-vector) and equations (1.104)-(1.113) on printed pp. 28-30 (dust, perfect fluids, energy-momentum tensor and its conservation); printed pp. 17-21 were inspected and found to contain tensor algebra and Maxwell's equations rather than momentum content, so the prose-scaffold locator 'pp. 17-21' is corrected here to pp. 27-30

contents.name: Chapter 1, printed p. 27, equations (1.98)-(1.99): four-velocity U^mu = dx^mu/dtau and the normalisation eta(U,U) = -1
contents.reason: The four-velocity definition and its normalisation are the established supplier of the worldlines-and-clocks pair (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration and thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition); this page consumes them as mathematical premises and mints nothing here.

contents.name: Chapter 1, printed p. 27, equations (1.100)-(1.101): p^mu = mU^mu, energy as the time component, rest frame E = mc^2, p^mu = (gamma m, v gamma m, 0, 0), small-v rest plus kinetic energy, and the frame dependence of energy
contents.support: Clauses (a)-(b) give the components (E/c, p), E = m gamma_w c^2 and p = m gamma_w w; the observer dependence of E and the invariance of m are clauses of the observer identities lemma and of the counterexample cex-sr-kinetic-energy-is-observer-dependent.

contents.name: Chapter 1, printed p. 27, equation (1.102): f^mu = m d^2x^mu/dtau^2 = dp^mu/dtau, the tensorial analogue of f = dp/dt
contents.support: The definition introduces the proper-time derivative of the four-momentum and names F = dot P the four-force, deriving no force law; the identity F = mA for constant mass is in the four-force identities lemma.

contents.name: Chapter 1, printed pp. 28-29, equations (1.104)-(1.110): number flux, dust and perfect-fluid energy-momentum tensors
contents.reason: Dust and perfect-fluid stress tensors are the declared subject of the forces-and-continuum pair, not of point-particle collision kinematics; nothing on this page depends on a chosen continuum model.

contents.name: Chapter 1, printed pp. 29-30, equation (1.113): conservation d_mu T^{mu nu} = 0, with the source's statement that it is not proved in general and follows from each matter model's equations of motion
contents.reason: The divergence balance for a continuum stress tensor and its finite-flux consequences are the forces-and-continuum pair's reserved content; the source's own remark that the general proof is omitted confirms it cannot serve as a supplier here.

contents.name: Chapter 1, printed p. 30: aside on the absence of a local gravitational-field energy-momentum tensor
contents.reason: The remark concerns general relativity and gravitational energy; this page has no gravitational field, and no claim about a gravitational stress tensor is made or needed in flat spacetime.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Mathematical Tripos Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision); Internet Archive copy of the original https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/hsr1000/part3_gr_lectures.pdf
sources.locator: Section 6.3 printed pp. 63-64 (PDF pp. 64-65), equations (6.17)-(6.19), and Section 7.4 printed pp. 86-87 (PDF pp. 87-88), the centre-of-momentum frame remark

contents.name: Section 6.3, printed pp. 63-64, equations (6.17)-(6.19): P^a = m u^a, g_ab P^a P^b = -m^2, and the observer-measured energy E = -g_ab(p) v^a(p) P^b(p)
contents.support: The definition of the observer energy E_n(P) = -c eta(P,n) and of the invariant mass m(P) = sqrt(-eta(P,P))/c is the c-retained flat-space form of these three equations, with the observer normalised to eta(n,n) = -1.

contents.name: Section 6.3, printed p. 64: no canonical contraction of vectors at different events in GR; an observer at p cannot measure the energy of a particle at q
contents.reason: This is a general-relativistic limitation of remote comparison; in the affine flat model displacement vectors live in the single vector space V, so the caveat neither constrains nor contributes to the flat particle kinematics developed here.

contents.name: Section 6.3, printed pp. 64-65: Maxwell and perfect-fluid stress tensors, the energy and momentum density measured by an observer, and local conservation of the energy-momentum current
contents.reason: Continuum stress tensors and current balance belong to the forces-and-continuum pair; this page treats finite lists of particle four-momenta and mints no field or continuum object.

contents.name: Section 7.4, printed pp. 86-87: choice of almost inertial coordinates with total three-momentum P_i = 0, the centre-of-momentum frame, and the statement that in it the total energy E is the total mass M
contents.support: The lemma proves in the flat model that a future timelike total Q has a centre-of-momentum frame with e_0 = Q/(Mc), that E_{e_0}(Q) = Mc^2, and that the frame is unique up to spatial rotations; the source states the equality only inside a linearised-gravity source calculation, which is not used as a proof route.

canonical.name: Design inventory (def): observer energy E_n, spatial momentum q_n, kinetic energy and invariant mass
canonical.support: All four quantities are defined explicitly with their dependence on P, n and the rest-mass parameter m, with units and physical identification left to the model conventions and postulates.

canonical.name: Design inventory (M04): the mass shell
canonical.support: The lemma proves E_n(P)^2 = m(P)^2 c^4 + c^2 |q_n(P)|^2 for future timelike P and the null identity E_n = c |q_n|, with positivity of the observer energy proved rather than assumed.

canonical.name: Design inventory (post): p = mU with m > 0 constant and additive isolated-collision balance, with a separate explicit premise for the massless case
canonical.support: The postulate adopts the mass parameter, P = mU, the observer measurement identification, isolated collision balance and the equation-of-motion form, with the massless case excluded and assigned to a separate premise.

canonical.name: Design inventory (pthm): collision kinematics and thresholds conditional on interaction assumptions
canonical.support: The physics theorem states the conditional physical mass shell, system mass, null-case and necessary-threshold claims, with explicit non-assertion of any interaction, cross section or probability.

canonical.name: S7 four-force identities: F = gamma (f . w/c, f), eta(P,F) = 0, dE/dt = f . w, and the variable-mass derivative
canonical.support: All four identities are proved in the inertial frame from P = mU, together with the caveat eta(P,F) = -m c^2 dm/dtau for a variable mass parameter.

canonical.name: S7 ideal massless particle as a separate primitive: nonzero future null momentum, E_n = c |q_n|, no rest frame, not m = 0 in mU
canonical.support: The postulate states the null four-momentum model and excludes the degenerate massive formula; the identity E_n = c |q_n| is supplied mathematically and the counterexample records why m = 0 in mU fails.

canonical.name: S7 system invariant mass, centre-of-momentum frame, M >= sum m, and the null-pair mass formula M = 2 sqrt(E1 E2) / c^2
canonical.support: The lemma proves the centre-of-momentum identity, the per-side inequality and its equality case, the two-leg formula M^2 = m1^2 + m2^2 + 2 m2 E / c^2, the general null-pair mass and the one-null-leg impossibility.

canonical.name: S7 covariant particle equation and mass-shell preservation for a stipulated smooth four-force
canonical.support: Clause (iv) adopts the equation-of-motion form only for a stipulated force and disclaims any force law or solution existence; the required orthogonality eta(U,F) = 0 for a constant mass is proved in the four-force identities lemma.
